panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel shows the overall habitus of a 16-month-old male consistent with the documented features of Fryns syndrome, including coarse facial features and general hypoplasia. B: Lateral view clearly shows dysmorphic features characteristic of Fryns syndrome, including a short and thick neck and micrognathia. C: Oral view reveals a cleft palate, a characteristic dysmorphic feature mentioned in the caption and text for this case of Fryns syndrome.

panels.figure_caption: Fryns syndrome with short thick neck, micrognathia, coarse face, hypoplasic extremities and cleft palate.
in_text_mentions: Preoperative evaluation of the 16-month-old 9 kg male, who was in the 8th percentile for weight and 2nd percentile for height, with FS diagnosis showed typical features of coarse broad face, broad and flat nasal bridge, cleft palate, micrognathia, short and thick neck, widely spaced nipples, and hypoplastic extremities (Figure 1).
